extraction.name: CIFAR-10 airbench
extraction.description: A set of training methods for CIFAR-10 that reach 94% accuracy in 3.29 seconds, 95% in 10.4 seconds, and 96% in 46.3 seconds on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU, including a novel derandomized alternating flip augmentation.
extraction.creator: Keller Jordan
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The paper uses the existing CIFAR-10 dataset, which contains 60,000 32x32 color images labeled as one of ten classes, divided into 50,000 training and 10,000 validation images.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: CIFAR-10 dataset (Krizhevsky et al., 2009), consisting of 60,000 32x32 color images across ten classes.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data augmentation includes random horizontal flipping (or alternating flip), 2-pixel random translation with reflection padding, and patch-whitening initialization of the first convolutional layer computed from the training distribution.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The training methods are developed specifically for CIFAR-10 and the paper notes that standard ImageNet trainings considered do not significantly benefit from horizontal flipping, limiting the generalizability of the alternating flip method.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and benchmarking neural networks on CIFAR-10; accelerating experimental iteration for researchers; enabling large-scale studies requiring many trained networks (e.g., data attribution, training variance studies).

description.evidence: we introduce training methods for CIFAR-10 which reach 94% accuracy in 3.29 seconds, 95% in 10.4 seconds, and 96% in 46.3 seconds, when run on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU.

isLiveDataset.evidence: The CIFAR-10 dataset contains 60,000 32x32 color images, each labeled as one of ten classes. It is divided into a training set of 50,000 images and a validation set of 10,000 images.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: The CIFAR-10 dataset contains 60,000 32x32 color images, each labeled as one of ten classes.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: CIFAR-10 (Krizhevsky et al., 2009) is one of the most popular datasets in machine learning... The CIFAR-10 dataset contains 60,000 32x32 color images, each labeled as one of ten classes.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: For data augmentation we use random horizontal flipping alongside 2-pixel random translation. For translation we use reflection padding... Following Page (2019); tysam-code (2023) we initialize the first convolutional layer as a patch-whitening transformation.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: We conclude that altemating flip improves over random flip for every training scenario where the latter improves over no flipping at all... we note that, surprisingly to us, the standard ImageNet trainings that we considered do not significantly benefit from horizontal flipping.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: One motivation for the development of these training methods is that they can accelerate the experimental iteration time of researchers working on compatible projects involving CIFAR-10. Another motivation is that they can decrease the cost of projects involving a massive number of trained networks.
